ags.intro: Control how the recruitment assistant works: model, tools, limits and guidance.
ags.enabled_hint: When off, the assistant is unavailable on every page.
ags.instructions_hint: Added to the assistant's instructions for every question, for example tone or what to keep in mind.
ags.examples_hint: One question per line. Shown when a conversation starts.
ags.model_hint: Leave these empty to use the model set on the server.
ags.key_keep: Leave empty to keep the current key
ags.key_hint: Stored encrypted and never shown again.
ags.key_unavailable: The key cannot be stored because the service key is not set on the server.
ags.temperature_hint: 0 to 2. Lower is more precise. Leave empty for the default.
ags.tools_hint: Choose what the assistant may use. Any change always needs your approval.
error.agent_proposal_minutes: Validity must be between 5 and 1440 minutes.
error.agent_daily_limit: The daily limit must be between 1 and 5000.
error.agent_history_turns: Messages remembered must be between 2 and 100.
error.agent_key_missing: The service key is not set on the server.
pers.reverse_hint: Agreeing with the statement lowers the trait score.
pers.likert_hint: Candidates answer on a five-point scale from strongly disagree to strongly agree. There is no right answer.
pers.norms_hint: Average and standard deviation of the item mean (1 to 5) in a reference group. With them, percentiles and normed stens are shown.
pers.added: {count} statements and a draft questionnaire were added. Review it, then publish it.
pers.no_profile: The questionnaire is not complete yet.
pers.note_scale: Scores are on a 1 to 10 scale from the candidate's answers, without reference norms. Traits are neither good nor bad; use them with interviews and other evidence, never on their own.
pers.note_norms: Percentiles and stens compare with the reference norms entered. Traits are neither good nor bad; use them with interviews and other evidence, never on their own.
error.trait_required: Choose the trait the statement measures.
error.norms_invalid: The norms are not valid: the mean is 1 to 5 and the SD above zero.
pers.model_hint.WorkplaceBigFive: Five dimensions, each the sum of its statements (5 to 25): 21 to 25 Very High, 16 to 20 High, 11 to 15 Moderate, 6 to 10 Low, 5 Very Low. Role profiles give a fit percentage.
pers.model_hint.WorkplaceType16: Four preference pairs (E or I, N or S, T or F, J or P). The higher pole in each pair gives a letter, and a tie goes to I, S, F or P. The four letters are the type.
pers.model_hint.BigFive: Each trait is the average answer on a 1 to 10 scale (sten), with reverse-scored statements. Add reference norms for percentiles. Suits the IPIP questionnaire.
pers.model_hint.SixteenPF: The sixteen factors are ready for scoring. The original 16PF questions are licensed by the publisher: add them to the question bank once licensed, with the factor code on each statement.
pers.note_sums: Each dimension is the sum of its answers (1 to 5 each). Use the profile with interviews and other evidence, never on its own.
pers.note_type: The type describes preferences, not abilities. Use it to guide interview questions, together with other evidence, never on its own.
roles.subtitle: What each position looks for in a personality questionnaire. Results show a fit for each active profile.
roles.note: Fit is one input to selection, alongside technical tests and structured interviews. Map every position you recruit for.
roles.types_hint: Strong Fit when the candidate's type is one of these, Moderate Fit when three of the four letters match one of them, otherwise Weak Fit.
roles.weights_hint: Fit = the weighted dimension scores out of 25, as a percentage. For example, 22, 23, 18, 20 and 19 with Project Manager weights give 84%.
error.role_weights_invalid: The weights must be 0 to 100 and add up to 100.
error.role_thresholds_invalid: Moderate Fit must start below Strong Fit, and Strong Fit at 100 or less.
error.role_profile_invalid: The role profile is not valid.
offer.terms_hint: Filled into the letter where the template has {terms}.
offer.print_hint: Choose "Save as PDF" in the print window to keep a PDF copy.
offer.no_template: There is no active offer letter template. Add one under Offer Templates.
offer.emailed: Saved. The offer letter was emailed to the candidate.
otpl.intro: Letters in Arabic and English. Pick one when making an offer; the default is used otherwise. When an offer is marked as sent, the Job Offer email includes the letter.
otpl.body_hint: A blank line starts a new paragraph. A line starting with "# " is a heading. Click a placeholder to insert it.
otpl.default_hint: Used when no template is picked for an offer.

mail.test_failed: The server {server} did not accept the email:
mail.server_intro: The server used to send all emails to candidates. The password is stored encrypted and never shown again.
mail.in_use_settings: Emails are sent through the server below.
mail.in_use_env: No server is set here, so emails use the server from the installation settings ({host}). Enter a server below to use it instead.
mail.in_use_none: No email server is set, so no emails are sent to candidates (account activation, invitations and so on).
mail.host_hint: For example smtp.office365.com. Leave empty to use the installation settings.
mail.password_kept: A password is stored. Leave empty to keep it.
mail.cannot_store: Passwords can only be stored once the installation has an AGENT_KEY.
mail.templates_intro: The wording of every email sent to candidates, in Arabic and English. Arabic-speaking candidates get the Arabic version and everyone else the English version.
mail.not_ready: No email server is set, so these emails are not sent. An administrator can set one under System, Email Server.
mail.events_hint: Sent automatically when something happens. Switch an email off to stop sending it.
mail.custom_hint: Wording HR can reuse when writing to a candidate. The assistant uses it when it drafts emails.
mail.required_hint: Candidates need this email to sign in, so it cannot be switched off.
mail.key_hint: Lowercase letters, numbers and underscores, for example documents_request.
mail.subject: Subject
mail.body_hint: A blank line starts a new paragraph. A paragraph that is only {link} becomes a button.
mail.event_hint.verify: Sent when a candidate creates a portal account, with the activation link.
mail.event_hint.reset: Sent when a candidate asks to reset their password, with the reset link.
mail.event_hint.application_received: Sent when a candidate applies for a job.
mail.event_hint.assessment: Sent when a candidate is invited to a test.
mail.event_hint.reexam: Sent when a candidate is given a new attempt and HR chooses to notify them.
mail.event_hint.interview_scheduled: Sent when an interview is scheduled.
mail.event_hint.offer_sent: Sent when an offer is marked as sent. {offer_letter} is replaced by the offer letter.
mail.event_hint.not_selected: Sent when an applicant's status is changed to Not Selected.
mail.log_intro: Every email sent to candidates. Failed emails are retried automatically six times; you can send one again after that.
mail.requeued: The email will be sent again shortly.
